5. Mr. M Fazlul Karim, in support of the Rule, submitted that the defendants-petitioners were in exclusive possession of the land in suit which was adjacent to their homestead where they grew different crops and as such the Court of appeal below was wrong in decreeing the suit reversing the judgment of the trial Court as in the DP Khatian Ext. A series the land was recorded in the name of the defendants-petitioners. It was also contended by him that Kamaluddin was a minor at the time of the purchase of the disputed land and he was a benamdar and had no right to transfer the entire land in favour of opposite party and no title has accrued to the opposite party under the kabala dated 22.3.72 in question Ext. A(1). He submitted that as the petitioners were in possession of the disputed land which is recorded in DP Khatian in their name and as Kamaluddin was only a co-sharer in the disputed land the lower appellate Court illegally decreed the suit as a whole. The learned Advocate for the petitioners further submitted that the land being ejmali property and other co-sharers being in possession jointly with the plaintiff-opposite party the decree for permanent injunction for the entire land is not sustainable in law as because a co-sharer cannot deprive other co-sharers from enjoyment of the property and the plaintiff-opposite party at best is entitled to a decree to the extent of his share of the land in dispute. 

 6. Mr. AKM Abdul Hakim, the learned Advocate appearing in opposition to the Rule, submitted that the Court of appeal below on a proper consideration of the exhibits namely Kabala Ext. A(1) dated 22.3.72, Ext. 3 series the rent receipts and Ext. A series, the PWs and BS Khatians and also considering oral evidence of the PWs and the DWs came to a finding that the plaintiff proved his case of exclusive possession in the disputed land. This finding as to possession being based on evidence on record can not be set aside, he submitted. It was further argued by him that it is not correct that a co-sharer in exclusive possession of a property is not entitled to get a decree for permanent injunction against the defendants until institution of a partition suit. He further submitted that even if transferee from a co-sharer is found in exclusive possession of the entire land which has been transferred to him in which others are also cosharers the purchaser is entitled to get a decree for permanent injunction against the other co-sharers without bringing a suit for partition. Mr. Hakim in support of his contention cited the case of Ahmed Miaji and others Vs. Eakub Ali and others, 12 DLR 708 and Muhammad Muzaffar Khan Vs. Muhammad Yusuf Khan, 11 DLR (SC) 78. I shall presently consider the decisions. 

 7. The instant suit is a suit for permanent injunction. In a suit for permanent injunction the plaintiff is required to prove his possession in the land in suit. For the purpose of determination of possession in such a suit the Court is required to arrive at a finding as to possession of the parties in the disputed land. No doubt it can look into the question of title incidentally. In this case the plaintiff sought permanent injunction in respect of 13 sataks of land appertaining to RS plot No. 457 and 13 sataks of land appertaining to RS plot No. 456. The plaintiff's claim is based on Kabala Ext. 1(a) dated 22.3.1972. In support of his case the plaintiff filed the kabala Ext. 1(a), the rent receipts Ext. 3 series showing payment of rent in respect of the land in suit and also examined witnesses including himself as PW1, PW2 is one Abul Faiz, the scribe of the kabala, PW3 is Rustam Ali Khan and PW4 is Siddique Ahmed. While defendants in support of their case filed certain documents namely Ext.A series, the PS and the BS Khatians and also examined witnesses. Defendant No. 1 was examined as DW 1 while DW 2 was one Mokbul Ali.
